The author's motive to illuminate the complexities of patriotism and the high cost of war is structurally embedded in the narrative through the characters' navigation of moral dilemmas and the repercussions of political choices. By grounding the political thriller in his own experiences as a war correspondent, Franklin uses the characters' struggles as a vehicle to explore these themes, thereby linking his intent to shed light on these issues directly to the thematic structure of the text.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
